## 開篇固定收益主論

6月26日，美債上漲。油價再度重挫、通膨預期指標降溫，加上科技業壓力重現，抵銷了聯準會仍遠未能宣布抗通膨勝利的證據。漲勢集中在中期券種：2年期殖利率下跌3.1個基點至4.093%，5年期下降3.7個基點至4.129%，10年期下滑2.3個基點至4.371%；30年期殖利率反而微升0.3個基點至4.865%。

10年期以內殖利率雖然下跌，曲線仍略為陡峭化。2年與10年期利差擴大0.8個基點至27.8個基點，2年與30年期利差則擴大3.4個基點至77.2個基點。長債表現落後，顯示眼前能源衝擊緩解及市場為科技股賣壓尋求避險，仍不足以消除較長期的通膨、供給與期限溢價風險。

10年期殖利率的組成變化，較符合溫和的通膨降溫交易，而非市場全面撤回對聯準會偏緊立場的定價。實質殖利率下降2.1個基點至2.159%，損益兩平通膨率卻僅下滑0.2個基點至2.212%。紐約聯準銀行的一項研究指標顯示，5月基礎通膨由修正後的3.7%降至3.4%；密西根大學調查中的家庭長期通膨預期也由3.4%降至3.3%。這些訊號有利美債曲線腹部，但兩者仍高於可讓通膨順利回到聯準會2%目標的水準。

油價是市場最主要的利多來源。儘管前一天有貨櫃輪遇襲，油輪仍持續通過荷莫茲海峽，WTI下跌3.74%至$69.23，布蘭特原油下跌4.34%至$71.99，兩項指標全週分別跌約9.6%及9.8%。這降低了未來整體通膨受到的推升力道；不過，明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari表示，更廣泛的物價壓力促使他預測今年升息一次。

科技市場則為美債帶來另一股需求，但尚未形成全面避險。費城半導體指數重挫5.29%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.09%，新興市場股票更創逾3個月來最差單週表現；不過，最大型科技公司以外的股票上漲，抵銷晶片股重挫，使S&P 500收盤幾乎持平。信用市場方面，整體上市債券基金也相對穩定，但SpaceX新發行的長天期債券相對美債出現異常龐大的損失。當日市場的核心是選擇性重新定價：能源及通膨壓力下降，使中期政府債受惠；長天期主權債與公司債則仍需為政策及融資不確定性提供額外補償。

## 通膨降溫有利美債曲線腹部

當日數據緩和近期通膨前景，投資人不必因此認定下一步政策必然是立即升息或迅速重返寬鬆，5年期券種因而領漲美債。其殖利率收於4.129%，全週下降10.4個基點；相較之下，2年期、10年期及30年期殖利率全週分別下跌8.7、8.4及3.4個基點。

紐約聯準銀行的多變量核心趨勢估計，帶來當日最明確的新增通膨降溫訊號。5月估計值由下修至3.7%的4月數據降至3.4%。其68%機率區間仍寬達3.0%至3.9%，而且這是研究模型，並非聯準會官方預測；不過，各主要組成項目均有改善。

不含住房的服務業仍是趨勢通膨高於疫情前水準的最大來源，其貢獻較疫情前平均值高出0.83個百分點，低於4月的0.91個百分點。核心商品的相應貢獻由0.67個百分點降至0.59個百分點，住房則由0.24個百分點降至0.16個百分點。各項貢獻全面下降之所以重要，是因聯準會關注的焦點已由單一能源衝擊，轉向商品與服務價格的持續性。模型顯示基礎通膨仍明顯高於目標，但未顯示其持續性在5月再度惡化。

密西根大學最終調查也提供了方向一致的家庭部門訊號。受訪者對未來5至10年的通膨預期由3.4%降至3.3%；消費者信心雖有改善，仍接近歷史低點。這項修正協助美股收復稍早部分跌幅，也減輕市場對能源衝擊進一步固化於長期預期的疑慮。不過，在通膨已連續逾5年高於聯準會目標後，該結果尚不足以證明預期已經正常化。

成長證據也不支持把美債漲勢強烈解讀為衰退交易。紐約聯準銀行研究人員對第2季實質GDP的即時預測，由6月19日的2.68%微升至2.71%。其50%機率區間為1.66%至3.88%，80%區間則為0.55%至4.89%，凸顯單點估計仍有高度不確定性。模型納入消費、所得、耐久財、住房及存貨的新數據，屬該行研究人員的研究成果，而非紐約聯準銀行或FOMC的官方預測。

另一項於6月19日至24日訪問86位經濟學家的調查，同樣描繪出通膨持續、就業轉強的經濟，而非需求突然斷裂。受訪者把第4季核心PCE年增率預測上調至3.2%，整體通膨預測則維持3.5%；在就業增幅轉強後，他們下調失業率預測並提高新增就業估計。預測中位數認為聯準會將按兵不動，直到2027年6月才降息，但部分受訪者預期2026年底前會升息。全年平均成長率估為2.1%，第2季成長預測也獲上修。

Kashkari的談話說明，為何較溫和的研究指標雖推動債市上漲，卻未重新開啟全面寬鬆交易。這位明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁表示，促使他在6月預測中納入一次升息的，是廣泛通膨，而不只是中東能源衝擊。他指出，5月PCE物價年增4.1%，漲價範圍也擴及多個類別。聯準會19位決策官員中有9位預測今年至少升息一次，顯示Kashkari屬於規模可觀的緊縮陣營，而非孤立的反對者；其立場明確取決於物價壓力擴散及通膨仍高於目標的證據。

現券交易仍然活躍，但不及6月25日。FINRA紀錄的美債面額交易額為$9,716億，較前一交易日下降21.5%；其中名目附息債交易額減少21.4%至$7,466億。逾3年至5年期以內券種的成交額下降24.8%，逾7年至10年期以內下降20.9%，逾20年期則減少33.5%。這些數字反映雙向成交，而非買賣方向，但顯示市場在消化前一天的數據與標售調整後，美債漲勢及曲線陡峭化發生於交易活動減少的環境。

每週期貨部位資料顯示，週五行情出現前，市場兩側已有規模龐大且方向相反的曝險。截至6月23日，資產管理機構淨多5年期美債期貨291萬口，槓桿基金則淨空217萬口。2年期美債期貨方面，資產管理機構淨多部位全週增加192,984口至202萬口，槓桿基金淨空部位為179萬口。這些數據無法證明週五的資金流向或投資人動機，但如此龐大的部位有助解釋，市場對通膨及聯準會的假設一旦改變，為何短端與曲線腹部會出現顯著調整。

## 油價下跌重塑歐洲利率定價，但鷹派條件仍在

原油再度下跌，使先前通膨衝擊的急劇反轉進一步延續。週五仍有油輪雙向通行荷莫茲海峽，包括滿載駛離波斯灣的船隻，以及沿阿曼海岸駛入的空船。Ever Lovely週四遭不明發射物擊中，成為美國與伊朗達成臨時和平協議以來首宗通報攻擊，但船運並未停止。

部分船東及船長重新評估是否通行，這次攻擊仍未阻止交通逐步正常化。布蘭特原油在週五國際盤一度交投於約$74，紐約收盤則為$71.99。對近期通膨而言，貨物持續運送的實際證據，比當日仍在延續的地緣政治不確定性更具影響力；布蘭特原油及WTI近1個月跌幅因而分別達27.71%及26.26%。

歐洲利率市場隨之下調對ECB緊縮幅度的預期。交易員自4月以來首次不再完全反映2026年底前升息25個基點；美伊戰爭初期，市場一度反映近4次升息。歐元區2年期通膨交換率回落至2.2%以下，4月時曾高於3%；德國10年期公債殖利率下降1個基點至2.85%，創3月10日以來最低。

ECB消費者調查強化了這項重新定價。歐元區家庭5月預期未來1年物價上漲3.5%，低於4月的4%；但3年期預期維持2.9%，5年期指標也仍為2.4%。調查於5月7日至6月1日進行，時間早於美伊協議及其後油價下跌。因此，數據顯示近期能源價格反轉前，短期預期便已緩解；較長期讀數未變，則保留了通膨可能固化的疑慮。

消費者預期未來1年經濟萎縮1.7%，較4月預期的2.2%降幅溫和，預期失業率則微升至11.3%。成長悲觀程度下降、1年期通膨預期大幅回落，而長期指標仍處高檔，這組合較直接支持放慢緊縮步調，尚不足以支持立即結束ECB的政策爭論。

下一批通膨數據預料將顯示，歐元區6月整體物價年增率由3.2%降至約3%；西班牙、法國及德國預計下降，義大利則可能上升。核心通膨預料維持2.6%。這項分歧是政策辯論的核心：能源下跌可以迅速壓低整體通膨，但憂慮服務價格及第二輪效應的官員，仍需看到基礎壓力也隨之減弱的證據。

ECB執行委員Isabel Schnabel在美國收盤後於週六發布的談話中，仍保留鷹派但書。她表示，食品、商品與服務通膨均面臨上行風險，先前的能源衝擊可能傳導至更廣泛的定價。和平協議雖降低不利情境的可能性，但她預期荷莫茲海峽逐步恢復通行期間，油價仍會持續高於先前水準，並重申為使通膨回到2%，可能仍須進一步升息。她也表示目前尚未出現薪資壓力跡象，意味眼下的疑慮集中於未來可能發生的價格傳導，而非已形成的薪資—物價螺旋。

相對利率前景改變，使美元即使週五下跌0.07%，較長期間仍獲支撐。美元指數收於101.36，全週上漲0.51%，全月上漲2.21%。摩根大通、摩根士丹利及紐約梅隆銀行等機構下調歐元預測；隨市場反映更鷹派的聯準會及較少的ECB升息，多家銀行認為歐元未來1年可能接近$1.10。這些預測仍取決於聯準會是否採取足夠的政策限制，以驗證利差走勢；擁擠的美元多頭部位及油價回落則可能拖慢美元升勢。

固定收益市場收盤後，地緣政治局勢兩度變化。美國國防部表示，美軍週五稍晚攻擊伊朗的飛彈與無人機儲存設施及沿岸雷達設施。Axios報導，到了週日，美國與伊朗已同意停止報復性攻擊，並計畫週二在卡達舉行會談。這些後續發展無法解釋週五美債收盤，卻決定了能源與通膨定價的下一個起點：油價跌勢能否延續，不僅取決於油輪是否持續通行，也取決於新一輪停火能否挺過有關荷莫茲海峽及更廣泛衝突的談判。

## 科技壓力由股票蔓延至長天期信用債

科技股賣壓仍相當集中，因此整體股價指數幾乎持平，但AI基礎設施週期曝險最高的市場承受沉重壓力。半導體指數週五下跌5.29%，全週重挫7.94%；Nasdaq 100下跌1.09%，S&P 500跌幅不到0.05%。南韓Kospi指數下跌5.8%，帶動MSCI新興市場股票指標當日下跌2.8%、全週下跌4.4%，創逾3個月來最差單週表現。

這波壓力反映市場日益區分兩類企業：目前因供給短缺而受惠的供應商，以及為未來產能籌資的公司。Apple調高產品價格，凸顯記憶體及儲存設備短缺正傳導至消費者成本；有關OpenAI可能延後首次公開發行的報導，則使其生態系投資人原先預期的上市時程延後。記憶體生產商及其他基礎設施供應商仍有定價能力，但超大規模雲端服務商與軟體公司，面臨更棘手的問題：資本支出何時能產生回報，以及回報規模有多大。

對債券投資人而言，最明顯的表現是SpaceX規模$250億的首次發債持續惡化。截至週五下午，相對美債的帳面損失擴大至約$3.6億。一家交易商的報價顯示，2056年到期債券的利差較發行時美債加175個基點最多擴大28個基點。初步訂單曾接近$900億，促使承銷商改善定價，但長天期債券後來實際上抹去了當時所有定價改善。

賣壓以20年期與30年期債券最為明顯，發行時需求最強的卻是5年期券種。交易員認為，部分逆轉來自追求短期交易收益的帳戶：這些資金原本期待債券上市初期上漲，利差收窄未能實現後便轉而賣出。避險部位調整及發行規模異常龐大也可能有所影響。無論技術性因素如何組合，這次變動幅度均使SpaceX有別於近期其他大型科技業發債。

例如，Nvidia的2046年及2056年到期債券，利差較發行時擴大約8個基點；Alphabet今年稍早出售的長天期債券則已收窄。儘管市場預期SpaceX未來數年現金流將為負，且Fitch把公司對Elon Musk的依賴視為重要評等限制，SpaceX仍進入投資級債市。其股票在發債前大跌後已經回穩，因此債券走弱反映市場針對債權人補償進行重新評估，而非股價同日再度崩跌所造成的機械式反應。

整體科技信用債環境也轉弱。截至週四，美國高評級科技債風險溢價升至79個基點，高於5月底的74個基點。截至週二，美國投資級債6月供給已達破紀錄的$1,750億，對買方形成壓力；AI相關借款可能進一步增加，也使市場擔心即使是評等良好的發行人，未來仍須提供更大的發行讓利。

發行股票未必能消除這項疑慮。Alphabet當月出售$850億股票，SpaceX則完成規模破紀錄的$750億首次公開發行。這些交易擴大了位於債權人之下、可先吸收損失的股權緩衝，但投資人也將其解讀為產業支出需求增長速度超過先前假設的證據。

摩根大通目前估計，至2030年AI與資料中心支出將達$5.5兆，較去年11月的預測增加約$4,000億。該行預期，未來5年將透過高評級債券市場籌措$2.1兆資料中心融資，高於原先估計的$1.5兆。這項修正使問題不再只是AI投資能否支持經濟成長，而是相關專案產生現金前，信用市場能吸收多少長天期曝險及發行人集中度。

SpaceX正體現這項矛盾。公司通報持有$1,008億現金，但S&P Global Ratings預期，截至明年底將消耗約$1,130億，2028年還會再消耗約$900億。因此，即使已完成規模異常龐大的資本募集，仍可能需要增發債券或股票。新股承擔風險時，債權人可獲得更多保護；但其上行空間有限，卻仍須承受數十年的技術、營運執行及再融資不確定性。

週五整體信用市場並未出現相當程度的壓力。投資級債券基金LQD持平，高收益債券基金HYG及JNK均微跌約0.06%，新興市場債券基金EMB則下跌0.02%。相較半導體股崩跌及SpaceX利差擴大，這些有限波動顯示，投資人正在區分資本密集的科技融資週期與整體公司信用環境。

不過，當週行情仍揭露槓桿曝險較廣泛的脆弱性。槓桿型交易所交易產品、龐大期貨部位、主要經紀商帳戶餘額及大型股票發行消耗銀行承作能力，使美股融資成本升至2024年12月以來最高。一旦融資環境收緊或擁擠部位解除，相關槓桿可能放大原本不大的價格變化。週五並未演變為全面流動性事件，VIX反而下跌2.54%至18.41；然而，股票槓桿、資本支出與信用債供給之間的交互作用，對利率前景已更加重要，因為它同時影響金融情勢與未來借款規模。

## 主權融資交易自有其抵押品風險

奈及利亞近幾週透過與第一阿布達比銀行簽訂、總額$50億的總報酬交換，首次動用約$15億。所得資金將協助再融資高成本債務並填補預算赤字，但這項結構以抵押曝險取代傳統無擔保借款，可能形成外匯壓力。

奈及利亞將提供價值相當於貸款133.3%的奈拉計價證券作為抵押品。第一批資金的利率為擔保隔夜融資利率加395個基點，其後借款則為SOFR加400個基點。國會議員4月批准交易時稱這些條件具競爭力，但總融資成本仍會隨美元利率及抵押安排變動。

國際貨幣基金警告，部分交易條款可能限制貨幣或匯率政策。Fitch表示，若國內殖利率上升或貨幣貶值，以奈拉資產擔保的交易可能觸發美元保證金追繳，進而形成外匯壓力。Moody’s則認為，同類交換交易會引進傳統商業借款沒有的風險。對截至12月底外債達$519億的主權國家而言，這項差異十分重要：現金立即到位，但未來資金需求可能正好在本地市場或匯率承壓時上升。

約翰尼斯堡則在截然不同的壓力下履行債券義務。該市償還一筆14.4億南非幣、約合$8,800萬、年票息11.455%的債券。這筆債券於2016年發行，其償還代表該市規模300億南非幣的國內中期票據計畫已完成贖回。即使該市積欠國營電力及供水事業數億美元，連道路維修所需燃料也缺乏資金，債券持有人仍優先於其他債權人獲得付款。

財政部長Enoch Godongwana威脅扣留每年80億南非幣的中央政府撥款，原因是約翰尼斯堡簽署一份他認為違法且無力負擔、價值103億南非幣的薪資協議。市長Dada Morero須在週五前說明為何應繼續撥款。該市也考慮發行新債，以處理2,200億南非幣的維修積壓。償還到期債券展現了維護市場融資管道的意願，卻未解決營運資源、薪資承諾及基礎設施需求之間的落差。

加拿大第1季公共帳目顯示，財政情勢雖沒有那麼緊迫，內部仍呈分歧。一般政府赤字較一年前擴大C$15億至C$164億，相當於GDP的2.1%，一年前為1.9%。聯邦政府赤字增加C$33億至C$194億，各省及地區政府合計赤字則縮減C$52億至C$182億。

一般政府整體淨負債下降C$260億，降幅4.6%，至C$5,381億；其占GDP比率也由17.9%降至16.5%。然而，排除社會保障基金後，淨負債增加4.3%至C$1.49兆，相當於GDP的45.6%。這項會計差異，把有利的合併資產負債表指標，與聯邦及省級預算更直接承擔的借款負擔區分開來。

亞洲週末公布的數據進一步顯示工業活動強勁，但現金流品質並不均衡。中國大型工業企業1至5月利潤增加18.8%至CNY3.144兆，僅5月便較一年前成長21.1%。採礦業利潤增加33.5%，製造業增加20%，公用事業則下降2.7%。營收成長5.5%，成本增加4.7%，利潤率提高0.63個百分點至5.56%。

資產負債表細節則沒有同樣全面強勁。應收帳款增加7.7%，製成品存貨上升8.8%，整體資產負債率提高0.3個百分點至58.2%。這份在週五美國收盤後發布的數據支持區域成長及企業獲利前景，但也顯示更多營運資金被未收帳款與存貨占用。

新加坡5月製造業報告也呈現集中於少數產業的擴張。產出較一年前增加13%，但經季節調整後較前月下降0.7%。排除生物醫藥製造業，產出年增17.7%、月增3.1%。受AI相關需求及半導體設備帶動，電子業及精密工程業分別成長35.8%及32.2%；生物醫藥產出萎縮24.2%，化學業下降11.5%，運輸工程業下跌5%。結果強化了亞洲科技資本支出週期依然強勁的判斷，但也說明其對整體需求的貢獻並不全面。

即使油價下跌有助改善國內通膨，新興市場資產仍對美國利率環境敏感。美國5年期殖利率與拉丁美洲同類殖利率的30天相關係數，從2月底的0.10升至0.49；與新興歐洲、中東及非洲的相關係數則由0.03升至0.43。美國與墨西哥5年期殖利率的相關係數6月一度超過0.8。因此，美元走強及美國實質利率上升，可能透過收緊外部融資環境抵銷低油價的好處，尤其會影響仰賴投資組合資金流入的經濟體。

哥倫比亞反映了這項矛盾。該國主權債相對美債的利差在總統大選前收窄，但選後一週每天均告擴大。相較之下，塞內加爾政府宣布計畫自明年起削減預算赤字後，其美元債券上漲。低油價普遍有利能源進口國，但從奈及利亞的抵押交換、約翰尼斯堡償債，到哥倫比亞選後走勢反轉，發行人層級的市場變化均顯示，財政執行與融資結構仍是決定性因素。

## 前瞻市場意義

歐洲首批考驗將於6月29日到來。西班牙初值CPI在美東時間03:00公布，歐盟執委會企業與消費者調查於05:00接續發布。西班牙通膨率預料將由3.6%下降；此前歐元區消費者信心初值為-17.7，執委會調查將提供更多細節。這些數據將顯示，能源價格下跌是否帶來足夠廣泛的緩解，足以驗證市場下調ECB升息定價。

ECB中央銀行論壇於6月29日美東時間15:00在辛特拉揭幕，並持續至7月1日。決策官員必須在油價及家庭短期通膨預期下降，與核心通膨預料維持2.6%、長期預期仍高於目標之間取得平衡。關鍵差異在於，官員會把這些持續偏高的指標視為再次升息的理由，還是在能源價格反轉逐步傳導至物價期間，把存款利率維持於2.25%。

美國6月29日的行程從美東時間10:30公布達拉斯聯準銀行製造業調查開始。財政部隨後於11:30標售$920億13週國庫券及$790億26週國庫券，兩者均於7月2日交割。6月30日接著標售$800億6週國庫券，7月1日供應17週券，7月2日則舉行例行4週及8週券標售。季末供給高度集中，將考驗假期融資期間的現金需求，但因沒有固定票息債券標售，市場缺乏可供比較的存續期訊號。

6月30日美國將於美東時間10:00公布JOLTS職缺及經濟評議會消費者信心，達拉斯聯準銀行零售調查則在10:30發布。亞洲時段稍早，日本將公布5月失業率及工業生產，澳洲央行也會發布6月會議紀錄。中國官方製造業、非製造業及綜合PMI前值分別為50.0、50.1及50.5，這將是首項廣泛檢視6月活動的數據，用以判斷大型工業企業利潤改善是否正擴散至更廣泛的經濟活動。

德國6月30日也將公布失業報告及CPI初值，同日還有英國第1季國民所得帳及經常帳終值。英國初值顯示實質GDP較前季成長0.6%。德國數據對德國公債尤其重要，因為工業前景轉弱及能源價格下降，正與食品、服務及商品通膨可能持續的疑慮相互角力。

7月1日將匯集全球製造業及通膨訊號。日本央行短觀調查將在日本央行6月升息後，更新企業景氣、物價預期及投資計畫；歐元區通膨初值則於美東時間05:00公布。其後從08:15至10:00，將陸續發布製造業PMI終值、ADP就業、紐約聯準銀行勞動市場緊俏度指標、美國營建支出及ISM製造業。這組數據將檢驗，具韌性的生產活動及AI相關投資，是否仍能產生足夠的就業與物價壓力，以維持市場對政策利率上升的預期。

美國利率市場最主要的催化因素，是因假期調整至7月2日美東時間08:30發布的就業報告，並與初領失業救濟金人數一同公布。6月非農就業、失業率及薪資將決定，聯準會的通膨疑慮是受到需求強勁進一步強化，還是因勞動市場轉弱而緩和。5月工廠訂單於10:00接續公布。數據發布後，11:30將舉行國庫券標售，SIFMA並建議市場於14:00提前收盤；固定收益市場7月3日休市。交易時段壓縮，意味市場面對重大的勞動數據意外或地緣政治再度升溫時，消化時間將更少。

能源仍是各市場共同的條件性風險。EIA截至6月26日當週的石油報告將於7月1日美東時間10:30發布，美國與伊朗也計畫週二在卡達會談。船運持續且雙方長久停止攻擊，將進一步降低整體通膨壓力。若再次遇襲、荷莫茲海峽出現新通行限制，或各方對通行條款意見不一，則會挑戰6月26日的美債漲勢；當日通膨補償成分幾乎未降，長端尤其容易受到能源溢價重現的衝擊。

overall_summary.headline: 油價與通膨訊號降溫帶動美債曲線腹部領漲，長端風險仍在
overall_summary.session_narrative:
6月26日，美債上漲。油價再度重挫、通膨預期指標降溫，加上科技業壓力重現，抵銷了聯準會仍遠未能宣布抗通膨勝利的證據。2年期殖利率下跌3.1個基點至4.093%，5年期下降3.7個基點至4.129%，10年期下滑2.3個基點至4.371%；30年期則微升0.3個基點至4.865%。曲線因而陡峭化，顯示近期通膨壓力緩解，仍未消除較長期的通膨、供給與期限溢價風險。

油輪持續通過荷莫茲海峽，WTI下跌3.74%至$69.23，布蘭特原油下跌4.34%至$71.99。紐約聯準銀行的一項基礎通膨指標5月降至3.4%，家庭長期通膨預期也降至3.3%。10年期實質殖利率下降2.1個基點，損益兩平通膨率卻僅下滑0.2個基點，較符合溫和的通膨降溫交易，而非市場全面撤回對聯準會偏緊立場的定價。Neel Kashkari預測升息一次，也凸顯政策風險尚未消失。

科技業壓力另外帶動美債需求，卻未演變為全面避險。半導體指數重挫5.29%，但S&P 500收盤幾乎持平，波動率也下降。整體信用市場相對穩定，SpaceX新發行的長天期債券相對美債卻出現異常龐大的損失，凸顯市場正選擇性擔憂長天期科技業融資。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries advanced on June 26 as another sharp fall in oil, cooler inflation-expectations measures and renewed technology-sector stress outweighed evidence that the Federal Reserve remains far from declaring victory over inflation. The rally was concentrated in intermediate maturities: the 2-year yield fell 3.1 basis points to 4.093%, the 5-year declined 3.7 basis points to 4.129% and the 10-year dropped 2.3 basis points to 4.371%, while the 30-year yield edged 0.3 basis point higher to 4.865%.

That distribution left the market with a modestly steeper curve despite lower yields through 10 years. The 2s10s spread widened 0.8 basis point to 27.8 basis points, and 2s30s steepened 3.4 basis points to 77.2 basis points. The long bond’s underperformance showed that relief from the immediate energy shock and demand for protection against the technology selloff did not remove longer-term inflation, supply and term-premium risk.

The 10-year decomposition was consistent with a measured disinflation trade rather than a wholesale retreat from the Fed’s tightening bias. The real yield fell 2.1 basis points to 2.159%, while the breakeven inflation rate eased only 0.2 basis point to 2.212%. A New York Fed research measure put underlying inflation at 3.4% in May, down from a revised 3.7%, and the University of Michigan survey lowered its longer-run household inflation expectation to 3.3% from 3.4%. Those signals supported the belly of the Treasury curve, but both remained above levels compatible with an uncomplicated return to the Fed’s 2% objective.

Oil provided the strongest market relief. WTI fell 3.74% to $69.23 and Brent dropped 4.34% to $71.99 as tankers continued moving through the Strait of Hormuz despite the previous day’s attack on a container ship. The declines took the benchmarks’ weekly losses to roughly 9.6% and 9.8%, respectively. That reduced the prospective headline-inflation impulse, even as Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said broader price pressure had led him to project one rate increase this year.

Technology markets supplied a separate demand impulse for Treasuries, but not a generalized flight from risk. The PHLX Semiconductor Index plunged 5.29%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.09% and emerging-market equities suffered their worst week in more than 3 months. The S&P 500 nevertheless finished almost unchanged as gains outside the largest technology companies offset the rout in chips. In credit, broad listed funds were also comparatively stable, while SpaceX’s newly issued long bonds sustained unusually large losses relative to Treasuries. The session was therefore defined by selective repricing: intermediate government bonds benefited from lower energy and inflation pressure, but long-duration sovereign and corporate exposures continued to demand compensation for policy and financing uncertainty.

## Inflation Relief Favors the Treasury Belly

The 5-year sector led the Treasury rally because the day’s evidence softened the immediate inflation outlook without requiring investors to assume that the next policy move must be either an imminent increase or a rapid return to easing. Its 4.129% yield was 10.4 basis points lower over the week, compared with weekly declines of 8.7 basis points in the 2-year, 8.4 basis points in the 10-year and 3.4 basis points in the 30-year.

The New York Fed’s Multivariate Core Trend estimate delivered the clearest incremental disinflation signal. The measure declined to 3.4% in May from an April reading revised down to 3.7%. Its 68% probability band remained wide at 3.0%-3.9%, and the estimate is a research model rather than an official Federal Reserve forecast, but the improvement extended across the major components.

Services excluding housing remained the largest source of excess trend inflation, contributing 0.83 percentage point above its pre-pandemic average, down from 0.91 point in April. The corresponding contribution from core goods fell to 0.59 point from 0.67, while housing’s contribution declined to 0.16 point from 0.24. The breadth of those decreases mattered because the Fed’s concern has shifted from a discrete energy shock toward persistence across goods and services. The model still placed underlying inflation materially above target, but it did not show that persistence worsening again in May.

The final University of Michigan survey supplied a compatible household signal. Respondents’ expected inflation over the next 5 to 10 years eased to 3.3% from 3.4%, while sentiment improved but remained near a record low. The revision helped U.S. equities pare an earlier decline and reduced concern that the energy shock was becoming further embedded in long-run expectations. It did not establish that expectations had normalized, particularly after more than 5 years of inflation above the Fed’s objective.

Growth evidence left less room for a strong recession interpretation of the Treasury rally. The New York Fed staff’s second-quarter real-GDP nowcast edged up to 2.71% from 2.68% on June 19. Its 50% probability interval extended from 1.66% to 3.88%, and the 80% interval from 0.55% to 4.89%, underscoring the uncertainty around the point estimate. The model incorporated new data on consumption, income, durable goods, housing and inventories, and remains a staff research output rather than an official New York Fed or FOMC forecast.

A separate survey of 86 economists conducted June 19-24 similarly described an economy with persistent inflation and firmer employment rather than an abrupt demand break. Respondents raised their forecast for fourth-quarter core PCE inflation to 3.2% from a year earlier, while leaving the overall inflation estimate at 3.5%. They lowered projected unemployment and increased job-growth estimates following stronger employment gains. The median forecast kept the Fed on hold until a rate cut in June 2027, although some respondents expected an increase before the end of 2026. Average growth for the year was put at 2.1%, with the second-quarter estimate revised higher.

Kashkari’s comments demonstrated why softer research measures produced a rally without reopening a broad easing trade. The Minneapolis Fed president said widespread inflation, not merely the Middle East energy shock, led him to include one increase in his June projection. He pointed to the 4.1% annual rise in May PCE prices and the spread of price increases across categories. Nine of the Fed’s 19 policymakers projected at least one increase this year, leaving Kashkari within a substantial tightening contingent rather than as an isolated dissenter. His preference was explicitly tied to evidence of broader pressure and inflation remaining above target.

Cash trading was active but lighter than on June 25. FINRA recorded $971.6 billion of Treasury par activity, down 21.5% from the preceding session, with nominal-coupon activity falling 21.4% to $746.6 billion. Turnover declined 24.8% in maturities above 3 and through 5 years, 20.9% beyond 7 and through 10 years, and 33.5% beyond 20 years. The figures describe two-way transactions rather than buying or selling direction, but they show that the rally and curve steepening occurred on reduced activity after the previous day’s data and auction adjustments.

The weekly futures-positioning snapshot showed substantial opposing exposures before Friday’s move. As of June 23, asset managers were net long 2.91 million 5-year Treasury futures contracts, while leveraged funds were net short 2.17 million. In 2-year futures, asset-manager net longs increased by 192,984 contracts over the week to 2.02 million, while leveraged funds’ net short position stood at 1.79 million. The data do not establish Friday’s flow or investor motive, but the scale of those positions helps explain why changing assumptions about inflation and the Fed can generate pronounced adjustments around the front end and belly.

## Cheaper Oil Reprices Europe, but Hawkish Conditions Survive

The renewed fall in crude extended a dramatic reversal in the inflation shock. Tankers continued transiting Hormuz in both directions on Friday, including loaded vessels leaving the Persian Gulf and empty carriers sailing inbound along the Omani coast. The flow persisted even after the Ever Lovely was struck by an unidentified projectile on Thursday, the first reported attack since the interim U.S.-Iran peace agreement.

Some owners and captains reconsidered passage, but the attack did not stop the gradual normalization of traffic. Brent traded around $74 during Friday’s international session before closing in New York at $71.99. The physical evidence that cargoes were still moving carried more weight for near-term inflation than the day’s continued geopolitical uncertainty, taking Brent’s 1-month decline to 27.71% and WTI’s to 26.26%.

European rate markets responded by reducing the expected scope of ECB tightening. For the first time since April, traders no longer priced a full 25-basis-point increase by the end of 2026, after nearly four increases had briefly been contemplated during the early phase of the U.S.-Iran war. The 2-year euro-area inflation-swap rate returned below 2.2%, compared with more than 3% in April, and Germany’s 10-year yield fell 1 basis point to 2.85%, its lowest since March 10.

The ECB’s consumer survey reinforced the repricing. Euro-area households expected prices to rise 3.5% over the following year in May, down from 4% in April. Expectations 3 years ahead stayed at 2.9%, however, and the 5-year measure remained at 2.4%. The poll ran from May 7 to June 1, before the U.S.-Iran agreement and subsequent fall in oil. It therefore showed near-term relief before the latest energy reversal, while the unchanged longer-horizon readings preserved concern about inflation becoming embedded.

Consumers also expected the economy to contract 1.7% over the coming year, less severe than the 2.2% decline anticipated in April. Their expected unemployment rate edged up to 11.3%. That combination—less pessimism on growth, a sharp fall in 1-year inflation expectations and still-elevated longer-term measures—supports a slower tightening path more directly than it supports an immediate end to the ECB debate.

The next inflation readings are expected to show euro-area headline price growth slowing to about 3% in June from 3.2%, with declines forecast in Spain, France and Germany and an increase in Italy. Core inflation is expected to remain at 2.6%. That split is central to the policy argument: falling energy can quickly reduce the headline rate, but officials concerned about services and second-round effects still need evidence that underlying pressure is following.

ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel preserved that qualification in comments released Saturday, after the U.S. close. She said food, goods and services inflation all faced upside risks and that the earlier energy shock could feed into broader pricing. Although the peace agreement made adverse scenarios less likely, she expected oil to remain persistently higher as Hormuz reopened gradually and reiterated that further rate increases may be needed to restore 2% inflation. She also said there was no sign of wage pressure yet, narrowing the current concern to prospective pass-through rather than an established wage-price spiral.

The changing relative-rate outlook continued to support the dollar over a longer horizon despite its 0.07% decline on Friday. The U.S. Dollar Index ended at 101.36, up 0.51% over the week and 2.21% over the month. Banks including JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and Bank of New York Mellon cut euro forecasts, with several seeing scope for the common currency to approach $1.10 over the next year as markets priced a more hawkish Fed and less ECB tightening. The forecasts remain conditional on the Fed delivering enough policy restraint to validate the rate differential; crowded bullish-dollar positioning and the retreat in oil could slow the move.

The geopolitical picture changed twice after the completed fixed-income close. The Pentagon said the U.S. struck Iranian missile and drone storage sites and coastal radar installations late Friday. By Sunday, the U.S. and Iran had agreed to halt retaliatory strikes and planned talks in Qatar on Tuesday, according to Axios. Those later developments cannot explain Friday’s Treasury close, but they define the next starting point for energy and inflation pricing: crude relief depends not only on visible tanker traffic, but also on whether the renewed truce survives negotiations over Hormuz and the wider conflict.

## Technology Stress Moves From Equities Into Long-Dated Credit

The technology selloff remained concentrated enough to leave the broad equity index almost unchanged but was severe in the markets most exposed to the AI infrastructure cycle. The semiconductor index dropped 5.29% on Friday and 7.94% over the week. The Nasdaq 100 lost 1.09%, while the S&P 500 slipped less than 0.05%. South Korea’s Kospi fell 5.8%, helping drive the MSCI emerging-market equity benchmark down 2.8% for the day and 4.4% for the week, its worst weekly performance in more than 3 months.

The pressure reflected a growing distinction between suppliers enjoying present scarcity and companies funding future capacity. Apple’s product-price increases highlighted the transmission of memory and storage shortages into consumer costs. Reports that OpenAI could delay its initial public offering weakened the expected timetable for investors in its ecosystem. Memory producers and other infrastructure suppliers still possessed pricing power, but hyperscalers and software companies faced harder questions about the amount and timing of returns on capital spending.

For bond investors, the clearest expression was the continued deterioration in SpaceX’s $25 billion debut offering. Paper losses relative to Treasuries increased to about $360 million by Friday afternoon. One dealer quoted the 2056 bonds as much as 28 basis points wider than their issue spread of 175 basis points over Treasuries. The long maturities effectively erased all the pricing improvement achieved by underwriters after initial orders had approached $90 billion.

The selling was most pronounced in the 20- and 30-year bonds, while demand at issuance had been strongest for the 5-year tranche. Traders attributed part of the reversal to fast-money accounts that entered the deal expecting an early gain and then sold when that tightening failed to materialize. Potential hedge adjustments and the unusual scale of the offering may also have contributed. Whatever the technical mix, the magnitude distinguished SpaceX from other recent large technology deals.

Nvidia’s 2046 and 2056 bonds, for example, had widened about 8 basis points from issuance, while longer-dated Alphabet securities sold earlier in the year had tightened. SpaceX entered the investment-grade market despite expectations of years of negative cash flow and dependence on Elon Musk that Fitch described as an important ratings constraint. Its equity had stabilized after falling sharply before the bond sale, leaving the debt weakness as a specific reassessment of creditor compensation rather than a mechanical response to another same-day collapse in the shares.

The broader technology-credit backdrop also weakened. Risk premiums on U.S. high-grade technology bonds reached 79 basis points as of Thursday, compared with 74 basis points at the end of May. June’s record $175 billion of U.S. investment-grade supply through Tuesday had already challenged buyers, and the prospect of further AI-related borrowing increased concern that even strongly rated issuers may need to pay wider concessions.

Equity issuance does not necessarily reduce that concern. Alphabet sold $85 billion of stock during the month, and SpaceX completed a record $75 billion initial public offering. Those transactions increase the capital cushion beneath bondholders, but investors also interpreted them as evidence that the industry’s spending requirements are growing faster than earlier assumptions.

JPMorgan now estimates that AI and data-center expenditure will reach $5.5 trillion through 2030, about $400 billion more than its November forecast. The bank expects $2.1 trillion of data-center financing to be raised in high-grade bond markets over the next 5 years, up from a previous estimate of $1.5 trillion. The revision turns the question from whether AI investment supports economic growth to how much duration and issuer concentration credit markets must absorb before the underlying projects generate cash.

SpaceX illustrates the tension. The company reported $100.8 billion of cash, but S&P Global Ratings expects it to consume about $113 billion through the end of next year and roughly another $90 billion in 2028. Additional debt or equity may therefore be needed despite the exceptionally large capital raises already completed. Bondholders benefit when new shares absorb risk, but their upside remains limited while they retain exposure to decades of technology, execution and refinancing uncertainty.

Broad credit did not show comparable distress on Friday. The LQD investment-grade fund was unchanged, while the HYG and JNK high-yield funds each slipped about 0.06%. The EMB emerging-market debt fund declined 0.02%. Those small moves, beside the collapse in semiconductor shares and SpaceX’s widening, showed investors discriminating between a capital-intensive technology financing cycle and general corporate-credit conditions.

The week nevertheless revealed a broader fragility around leveraged exposure. Financing costs for U.S. equities rose to their highest since December 2024 as leveraged exchange-traded products, large futures positions, prime-broker balances and major share offerings consumed bank capacity. The resulting leverage can amplify relatively small price moves when funding tightens or crowded positions unwind. Friday’s market did not become a generalized liquidity event—the VIX actually fell 2.54% to 18.41—but the interaction between equity leverage, capital expenditure and credit supply has become more important to the rates outlook because it affects both financial conditions and the scale of prospective borrowing.

## Sovereign Funding Trades Carry Their Own Collateral Risks

Nigeria obtained about $1.5 billion in recent weeks from the first draw under a $5 billion total-return swap with First Abu Dhabi Bank. The proceeds will help refinance expensive obligations and cover a budget deficit, but the structure replaces conventional unsecured borrowing with a collateralized exposure that can create foreign-exchange pressure.

Nigeria will provide naira-denominated securities worth 133.3% of the loan as collateral. The first tranche is priced at 395 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, with subsequent borrowing at SOFR plus 400 basis points. Lawmakers described those terms as competitive when approving the transaction in April, but the all-in cost will continue to vary with dollar rates and the collateral arrangement.

The International Monetary Fund has warned that parts of the deal could constrain monetary or exchange-rate policy. Fitch said dollar margin calls against naira collateral could generate foreign-exchange pressure if domestic yields rise or the currency weakens. Moody’s has argued that comparable swaps introduce risks absent from traditional commercial borrowing. The distinction is important for a sovereign with $51.9 billion of external debt at the end of December: the cash arrives immediately, while the future funding demand can rise precisely when local markets or the exchange rate are under stress.

Johannesburg met a bond obligation under very different pressure. The city repaid a 1.44 billion rand, or $88 million, bond carrying an 11.455% annual coupon. Issued in 2016, it completed redemption of the municipality’s 30 billion rand domestic medium-term-note program. Payment put bondholders ahead of other creditors even as the city owed state power and water utilities hundreds of millions of dollars and lacked funds for road-maintenance fuel.

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana threatened to withhold 8 billion rand of annual state funding because Johannesburg signed a 10.3 billion rand wage agreement that he considers illegal and unaffordable. Mayor Dada Morero was given until Friday to explain why the transfer should continue. The municipality is also considering new bond sales to address a 220 billion rand maintenance backlog. Repayment of the maturing security demonstrated a willingness to protect market access, but it did not resolve the mismatch between operating resources, wage commitments and infrastructure needs.

Canada’s first-quarter public accounts presented a less acute but still divided fiscal picture. The general-government deficit widened by C$1.5 billion from a year earlier to C$16.4 billion, or 2.1% of GDP, compared with 1.9%. The federal deficit increased C$3.3 billion to C$19.4 billion, while the aggregate provincial and territorial shortfall narrowed C$5.2 billion to C$18.2 billion.

Headline general-government net debt fell C$26 billion, or 4.6%, to C$538.1 billion and declined to 16.5% of GDP from 17.9%. Excluding social-security funds, however, net debt rose 4.3% to C$1.49 trillion, equivalent to 45.6% of GDP. The accounting difference separates a favorable consolidated balance-sheet measure from the borrowing burden more directly associated with federal and provincial budgets.

Asian releases over the weekend added evidence of strong industrial activity with uneven cash-flow quality. China’s large industrial enterprises reported an 18.8% increase in profits during January-May to CNY3.144 trillion, with May alone up 21.1% from a year earlier. Mining profits rose 33.5% and manufacturing profits 20%, while utilities declined 2.7%. Revenue increased 5.5%, costs rose 4.7% and the profit margin improved 0.63 percentage point to 5.56%.

The balance-sheet detail was less uniformly strong. Receivables grew 7.7%, finished-goods inventories increased 8.8% and the aggregate asset-liability ratio rose 0.3 percentage point to 58.2%. The release, published after Friday’s U.S. close, supports the regional growth and corporate-earnings outlook but also shows more working capital tied up in unpaid bills and inventories.

Singapore’s May manufacturing report displayed a similarly concentrated expansion. Output increased 13% from a year earlier but fell 0.7% on a seasonally adjusted monthly basis. Excluding biomedical manufacturing, production rose 17.7% annually and 3.1% on the month. Electronics grew 35.8% and precision engineering 32.2%, led by AI-related demand and semiconductor equipment. Biomedical output contracted 24.2%, chemicals declined 11.5% and transport engineering fell 5%. The result reinforced the strength of the Asian technology-capital cycle while showing why its contribution to broader demand cannot be treated as uniform.

Emerging-market assets remain sensitive to the U.S. rate backdrop even where lower oil improves domestic inflation. The 30-day correlation between U.S. 5-year yields and comparable Latin American yields increased to 0.49 from 0.10 at the end of February; for emerging Europe, the Middle East and Africa, it rose to 0.43 from 0.03. The U.S.-Mexico 5-year correlation exceeded 0.8 during June. A stronger dollar and higher U.S. real rates can therefore offset cheaper energy by tightening external financing conditions, particularly for economies dependent on portfolio inflows.

That tension was visible in Colombia, where sovereign spreads over Treasuries widened each day during the week after narrowing ahead of the presidential election. Senegal’s dollar bonds, by contrast, advanced after the government announced plans to reduce its budget deficit beginning next year. Lower oil offers broad relief to importers, but the session’s issuer-level moves—from Nigeria’s collateralized swap to Johannesburg’s repayment and Colombia’s post-election reversal—showed that fiscal execution and funding structure remained decisive.

## Forward Market Significance

The first European tests arrive June 29. Spain’s flash CPI is due at 03:00 ET, followed by the European Commission’s business and consumer survey at 05:00 ET. Spain’s inflation rate is expected to ease from 3.6%, while the commission survey will add detail after flash euro-area consumer confidence registered -17.7. The releases will indicate whether lower energy is producing broad enough relief to validate the reduction in ECB hike pricing.

The ECB Forum on Central Banking begins in Sintra at 15:00 ET on June 29 and continues through July 1. Policymakers must reconcile the fall in oil and short-term household inflation expectations with core inflation expected to remain at 2.6% and longer-run expectations still above target. The important distinction will be whether officials treat those persistent measures as grounds for another increase or as reasons to hold the deposit rate at 2.25% while the energy reversal works through prices.

The U.S. calendar opens June 29 with the Dallas Fed manufacturing survey at 10:30 ET. Treasury then auctions $92 billion of 13-week bills and $79 billion of 26-week bills at 11:30, both settling July 2. An $80 billion 6-week bill sale follows June 30, with 17-week supply on July 1 and regular 4- and 8-week auctions on July 2. The concentrated quarter-end schedule will test cash demand across the holiday funding window without a fixed-rate coupon auction to provide a comparable duration signal.

June 30 brings U.S. JOLTS vacancies and Conference Board consumer confidence at 10:00 ET, followed by the Dallas Fed’s retail survey at 10:30. Japan releases May unemployment and industrial production earlier in the Asian day, while the Reserve Bank of Australia publishes minutes from its June meeting. China’s official manufacturing, nonmanufacturing and composite PMIs, previously at 50.0, 50.1 and 50.5, will provide the first broad June check on whether the profit improvement at large industrial companies is translating into wider activity.

Germany’s unemployment report and flash CPI are also due June 30, alongside the U.K.’s final first-quarter national accounts and current-account figures. The preliminary U.K. estimate showed real GDP growth of 0.6% from the preceding quarter. Germany’s releases will be particularly important for Bunds because weaker industrial prospects and lower energy prices are competing with concern that food, services and goods inflation may remain persistent.

July 1 concentrates the global manufacturing and inflation signals. The Bank of Japan’s Tankan will update corporate conditions, price expectations and investment plans after the BOJ’s June increase. Euro-area flash inflation follows at 05:00 ET. Final manufacturing PMIs, ADP employment, the New York Fed’s labor-market-tightness indicators, U.S. construction spending and ISM manufacturing then run from 08:15 through 10:00 ET. The combination will test whether resilient production and AI-related investment are still generating enough employment and price pressure to sustain expectations for higher policy rates.

The principal U.S. rates catalyst is the holiday-shifted employment report at 08:30 ET on July 2, released with initial jobless claims. June payrolls, unemployment and wages will determine whether the Fed’s inflation concern is being reinforced by demand or moderated by a weaker labor market. May factory orders follow at 10:00. The data arrive before the 11:30 bill auctions and a SIFMA-recommended 14:00 early close; fixed-income markets are closed July 3. That compressed session will leave less time to absorb a material labor surprise or renewed geopolitical escalation.

Energy remains the common conditional risk. The EIA petroleum report for the week ended June 26 is due July 1 at 10:30 ET, while U.S.-Iran talks are planned in Qatar on Tuesday. Continued shipping and a durable halt to strikes would reinforce the decline in headline inflation pressure. Another attack, new restrictions on Hormuz traffic or disagreement over transit terms would challenge a Treasury rally whose inflation-compensation component barely declined on June 26, leaving the long end particularly exposed to any renewed energy premium.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury belly rallies as oil and inflation signals cool, while long-end risks persist
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries advanced on June 26 as another sharp fall in oil, cooler inflation-expectations measures and renewed technology-sector stress outweighed evidence that the Fed remains far from declaring victory over inflation. The 2-year yield fell 3.1 basis points to 4.093%, the 5-year declined 3.7 basis points to 4.129% and the 10-year dropped 2.3 basis points to 4.371%, while the 30-year edged 0.3 basis point higher to 4.865%. The resulting curve steepening showed that near-term inflation relief did not remove longer-term inflation, supply and term-premium risk.

WTI fell 3.74% to $69.23 and Brent dropped 4.34% to $71.99 as tankers continued moving through the Strait of Hormuz. A New York Fed measure of underlying inflation declined to 3.4% in May, and longer-run household inflation expectations eased to 3.3%. The 10-year real yield fell 2.1 basis points, while breakeven inflation eased only 0.2 basis point, consistent with a measured disinflation trade rather than a broad retreat from the Fed’s tightening bias. Neel Kashkari’s projection of one rate increase underscored the remaining policy risk.

Technology stress supplied a separate Treasury demand impulse without becoming a generalized flight from risk. The semiconductor index plunged 5.29%, but the S&P 500 finished almost unchanged and volatility fell. Broad credit remained comparatively stable, while SpaceX’s newly issued long bonds suffered unusually large losses relative to Treasuries, highlighting selective concern about long-duration technology financing.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields declined through 10 years, led by the 5-year sector, as crude retreated and inflation expectations softened, but the 30-year yield rose as Fed, supply and term-premium risks persisted.
